rationale: Focused knockout screens of 1,131 transcription factors (Brie-derived, 4,732 guides, 200 non-targeting) in ILCs differentiated in vitro from Cas9 reporter-mouse progenitors (Mef2d paper, Science 2024). GEO deposits four multiplexed count files; each lib_data file's pool.k is row k of the matching screen_list, and the screen lists themselves mark the two pools of each screen the authors compared (columns Screen and Bin, P or N). prepare.R takes exactly those pools: IL-13 tdTomato screens S17 (tomp vs linn) and S25 (Tp vs Neg), and GATA3/T-bet reporter screens S31 (ILC2 vs NK) and S35 (GATA3 vs TBET). This assignment differs from a reading of the GSM titles alone (S25 negative could be S25_Tn, S31 T-bet could be S31_ILC1); the authors' own P/N flags were used, and the IL-13 result reproduces the paper's named regulators (8 of 10 in the BARCS top 10), which supports it. The two sorted populations of a screen come from one infected culture, so screen is a paired term: ~ screen + population, 4 libraries, 1 residual df per analysis. Positive regulators are depleted in the positive population (Tom+ or GATA3+). The paper ran caRpools Wilcoxon tests per screen against non-targeting guides and combined screens with Fisher's method; the IL-13 screen is the primary comparison here and the GATA3 screen a second analysis because the paper's main claim (Mef2d) rests on both.
